             Dudhnoi College
       Dudhnoi, Goalpara, Assam – 783124
              (www.dudhnoicollege.ac.in)
 FROM THE PRINCIPAL’S DESK
     “Education is the most powerful weapon which you can use to change the world.”
                                                                      -Nelson Mandela




My dear students,
        On behalf of Dudhnoi College family, I feel proud to welcome you to Dudhnoi College, the premier
higher educational institution in the Goalpara District. This institute of higher education was established
on 4th August, 1972 with P. U. Course in Arts stream. Later on, Science and Commerce streams were
added in 1985 and 2015 respectively. I offer my sincere tribute to the noble persons of the locality without
whose vision and mission, this institution would not have seen the light of the day.
        Thanks to the honourable president and members of the Governing Body, teaching and non-
teaching staff of the College, who have given quality and consistency through their efforts. Their hard
work and sacrifices have helped in shaping the lives of students of this college. After joining the College
on 10th July, 2018 as Principal I have been trying to do better in the field of teaching, learning, research
and other corporate activities.
        I hope like other educational institution, Dudhnoi College will also be a greater partner in building
up the society and nation.
        Thanking You.
                                                                                  Dr. Lalit Chandra Rabha
                                                                                                   Principal,
                                                                                            Dudhnoi College
 FROM THE DESK OF ACADEMIC IN-CHARGE




Dear students,
        Education is a process of providing learning experiences to obtain knowledge, understanding,
skills and awareness with desirable attitudinal changes about one’s relationship with natural and
manmade environment. Education actually includes the training of the intellect and also the refinement
of the heart and the discipline of the spirit of the learner. At present the role of a college is not only to
trail academic excellence but also to develop its students to be critical thinkers, lifelong learners and
fecund members of an ever-changing society.
        Our college provide holistic student-centric environment for development of students in
multifarious activities. We try to instil the values of respect and encourage the students to channelize
their potential in the pursuit of excellence and in strengthening the foundation of real success.
        As our starling academic institution step into this new academic year with full hope and dreams
to climb to the top, I request all the students to properly utilize the facilities offered in the college and
mould their lives through the learning resources of the college that will support to develop them as leading
citizens of the nation.

      I firmly believe that, persistent determination, unbeatable hard work and invincible patience will
always help one to overcome all odds and challenges of life.

                                                                                          Dr. Dipali Deka
                                                                                       Academic In-Charge,
                                                                                          Dudhnoi College

VISION OF THE COLLEGE:




                                            The vision of Dudhnoi College is “to disseminate the knowledge of higher

                                 education among the needy section of the society and to become a frontrunner in teaching,

                                 learning and research, so that the fullest potential of the students may develop enabling

                                 them to compete with modern day challenges and opportunities, along with the quality of

                                 leadership that may inspire them to work for the advancement of the society and the nation”




                                 The mission of the College is as follows:
                                 ➢ To be a centre of higher learning through which quality education can be imparted to
       MISSION OF THE COLLEGE:




                                   the students by adopting best of the best practices.
                                 ➢ To mould intellectually competent, morally upright and socially committed persons
                                   capable of building a more human social order.
                                 ➢ To motivate the students to pursue higher education, appear in competitive exams, and
                                   other value-added programmes for their holistic development.
                                 ➢ To extend its activities to address environmental, social and cultural concerns in the
                                   region and promote free enquiry and life-long learning.
                                 ➢ To provide an environment to both the teachers and learners for developing the fullest
                                   potential by combining talents, skills and values in the field of culture and sports along
                                   with education.
                                 ➢ To generate and inculcate the leadership quality among the students for the
                                   advancement of the society and the nation by way of co-curricular and outreach
                                   extension programme.

 Section A. Dudhnoi College at a Glance:

       Dudhnoi College is the manifestation of
the collective dreams of the people of the locality
and   the   result   of   their    aspirations   and
perspirations. The College is located in Dudhnoi,
which is now headquarter of the Rabha Hasong
Autonomous Council. It is 110 km away from
Assam’s capital Dispur (Guwahati) and 42 km
from district headquarter Goalpara.

       The College had a modest beginning with only Pre-University (Higher Secondary) classes of Arts
stream in 1972. Degree classes of Arts stream started in 1974. Later on, Science and Commerce streams
were added in the session 1985-86 and 2015-16 respectively. Presently the College has 19 different
departments offering both Honours (Major) and Regular/General (Minor) Courses.

       The College has a pristine green and serene campus spreading over a vast area of 33.05 acres. A big
horse-shoe shaped pond runs around the main building. A foot-bridge over the pond enhances the beauty
of the college.

A-1. Facilities available in the College:

 1) Central Library: Library facility is available to all
      students and faculty members. Presently our library has more
      than 21,600 books covering different subjects including
      general studies and reference. In addition, one can access
      more than 9000 e-journals and 97,000 e-books through N-List
      (INFLIBNET). Moreover, The College also boast a Digital
      Library.
            The library has separate spacious reading rooms for students and faculties. It also has internet
      and Xerox facility. The library is completely digitised and presently working towards building audio-
      visual learning materials.
            The College library is open from 9 am to 4.30 pm in all working days.


 2) Central Computer Laboratory: The College has a Central Computer Laboratory in the
      Department of Computer Science with 50 computers. Apart from this every department has their own
      computer.
            Small separate computer lab is also available in some departments on the basis of requirement.
 3) ICT Equipped Modern Classrooms and Laboratories: The College has many
    classrooms equipped with modern audio-visual facility. Well-equipped modern laboratory facilities
    are available in different departments for effective teaching-learning.
4) Language Laboratory: The College has a fully equipped modern computerised Language
    Laboratory. There are 13 Computers in the Language Laboratory.
5) Hostel Facility: The College has separate well equipped hostels for Boys and Girls.
  i. Boys’ Hostel: The boys’ hostel has 80 seats. It has all modern amenities like twin-sharing rooms,
     electric fans, modern toilet facilities and running water. The hostel has own mess-hall and the mess
     is managed by boarders themselves under the supervision of the Superintendent.
  ii. Girls’ Hostel: The hostel at present has seats for 100 girls. It
     is fully secured with a surrounding high concrete wall. It has
     all modern amenities like twin-sharing rooms, electric fans,
     modern toilet facilities and running water. The hostel also has
     mess-hall and the mess is managed by boarders themselves
     under the supervision of the Superintendent.
6) Facilities for Physical Fitness:
    i.    Play Ground: The College has a large outdoor playground. Facilities of all sorts of outdoor
          games and sports are available. It also has an outdoor basketball court. A pavilion/spectator’s
          gallery covers one side of the field.
          The College has a MoU with Assam Cricket Association for the playground.
                                         ii.   Indoor Stadium: The College has a quite spacious modern
                                               indoor stadium along with spectators’ gallery.
                                        iii.   Gymnasium: The College has a fully equipped gymnasium
                                               with modern equipment. Some of the equipment available in
                                               the gymnasium are: Smith Machine, Cross Cable, Pee Dee Fly
                                               Machine, Leg Press and Hack Squat and Back Pull Down etc.
7) Students’ Common Room: The College has separate Boys’ and Girls’ common rooms.
  i. Boys’ Common Room: The boys’ common room has recreational facilities like carom and other
     board games and drinking water. It also has washroom facilities with running water.
  ii. Girls’ Common Room: The girls’ common room has recreational facilities like carom and other
     board games and drinking water. It also has washroom facilities with running water.
8) Parking Facilities: The College has separate parking shades for students and faculties. The
    covered parking area has separate provisions for bicycle, motorcycle/scooter and car parking. There
    is enough space for visitors parking also.
  9) Canteen Facilities: The College has a large well-furnished Canteen with separate seating area for
     faculties and students. The Canteen is managed by Canteen Committee. It provides balanced healthy
     food in reasonable costs. It also has running water facilities.
 10) Drinking Water: Clean and safe drinking water is available in the College for students and staff.
     Modern water filters are fitted in various departments and different locations of the College.

A-2. Courses offered in the College:

  a. The College offers following fulltime Higher Secondary Courses:
       i.   Higher Secondary (10+2) in Arts.
      ii.   Higher Secondary (10+2) in Science.
     iii.   Higher Secondary (10+2) in Commerce.
  b. The College offers following fulltime Undergraduate Courses under NEP-2020:
       i.   B. A. (Major).
      ii.   B. Sc. (Major).
     iii.   B. Com. (Major).
     iv.    B. A. (General/Minor).
      v.    B. Sc. (General/Minor).
     vi.    B. Com. (General/Minor).
  c. The College offers:
       i.   Post Graduate Course (Arts) through Distance and Open Learning Programme under GUCDOE
            (Gauhati University Centre for Distance and Online Education), Assam.
      ii.   Under Graduate and Post Graduate Course (Arts) through Distance and Open Learning
            Programme under KKHSOU (Krishna Kanta Handiqui State Open University), Assam.
     iii.   Apart from these, the College also offer various Add-on Courses like Certificate Courses,
            Diploma Courses and training programme etc.

 A-2.2. Undergraduate Courses:

        The College offer undergraduate courses in three streams
under Gauhati University. These FYUGP-NEP courses are BA (Arts
stream), BSc (Science Stream) and BCom (Commerce Stream). All
these coursed are four-year course under New Education Policy and
have provisions for multiple entry and exit as per GU rule.

A-2.2.1: Course Structure of Four-Year Undergraduate Programme (FYUGP-NEP):

A-2.2.1.1: Important Points about FYUGP-NEP:

   1. FYUGP-NEP is a 4-year Undergraduate Programme that leads to Bachelor Degree in different
      subjects and streams.
   2. The course has provisions for multiple entry and multiple exits. A student may:
                                           i. Exit the programme after one year with a Certificate
                                          ii. Exit after two years with a Diploma
                                         iii. Exit after three years with a Bachelor Degree with Honours
                                         iv. Exit after four years with a Bachelor Degree (Honours) with
                                               Research.
                                        (NB-1: Any student who leave the course in the middle, i. e. after
                                        completing 1, 2 or 3 years, have the option of re-joining the course
                                        on a later date and complete the rest of the course.
              NB-2: Any student who wants to exit before completion of 3 years, MUST complete an
              additional Vocational Course of 4 credits.)
   3. If a student exits the FYUGP-NEP after 3 years, he/she will need to take admission into the first
      year of a Master Degree, which is a 2-year degree programme. However, if a student fully completes
      an FYUGP-NEP (i. e., exists after four years), he/she needs to take admission into the second year
      of a Master Degree and needs to study only one year to get a Master Degree.
   4. The whole FYUGP-NEP courses are divided into two parts — (i) Core Courses and (ii) Common
      Courses. The minimum credit allocation for a 3-year programme is 84 credits in Core Courses and
      36 credits in Common Courses, which comes to a total of minimum 120 credits for a 3-year
      programme.
   5. In the first and second semester, a student studies three different core subjects – one paper of each
      subject per semester. Besides, they need to study four
      common subjects.
   6. In the third semester, a student may select one core subject
      as Major subject and other two as Minors.
   7. A Student will have the option of changing the Major in
      fourth semester to any one of the other two Minors, even if
      one has already declared a Major in the third semester.
      However, this is subjected to the availability of seat in the
      concerned department.

 Section B. General Information and Guidelines for Students:

B-1: Eligibility and Admission Procedure:

 1.   The College follows relevant guidelines and regulations of
      affiliating authorities like GU, AHSEC etc. regarding
      eligibility and minimum qualification for enrolment in any
      courses. Therefore, a student must check the relevant section of the affiliating institutions for the
      minimum qualification and any pre-requisite for every course before applying in the college.
 2.   Admission is given strictly on the basis of merit.
 3.   Aspiring students may apply for admission in Dudhnoi College through online portal by filling up
      requisite forms and paying the prescribed application fee.
 4.   The students will then have to appear for selection interview, on prescribed date, time and place,
      along with all necessary testimonials in original.
 5.   The admission process of the selected students will be over only after payment of all required fee
      through any of available online payment method.
 6.   Students whose parents’ total annual income is less than 2 lakhs rupees are admitted under the Assam
      Government’s Fee waiver scheme. Students seeking admission under this scheme must produce
      parents’ original income certificate issued by competent authority at the time of selection interview
      (certificate should not be more than one year old). Moreover the student must be a permanent resident
      of Assam.
 7.   During the admission, the College will follow the relevant Government Rules and Regulations
                                        regarding reservation.
                                         8.   All payments to the college are strictly cashless.
                                         9.   The decision of the Admission Committee is final and binding
                                              in case of selection and admission of a student.
                                         10. Students migrating from other universities and Boards must
                                              produce migration certificate and pay migration fee as per rule.

B-2: Change of Subject:

      Admitted Students may change their combination of subjects within one month from the date of
admission in Higher Secondary First Year. The Undergraduate students may change the Major subject in
Semester-IV after they select a subject as Major in Semester-III. However, such changes are subjected to
availability of seat and approval of concerned departmental HoD and Admission Committee.
 B-3: Attendance:

      Attendance in Higher Secondary classes (both theory and practical) is compulsory. Students with less
than 75% attendance will be dis-collegiated and will be barred from appearing in the Final Examination as
regular students.
                                               In Undergraduate Degree courses, the student must earn full
                                        credit in Core Courses (Major and Minor) and Common Courses
                                        [Ability Enhancement Courses (AEC), Skill Enhancement Courses
                                        (SEC), Multidisciplinary (MDC) and Value Added Course (VAC)].
                                        A student must have minimum 75% attendance. (Attendance means
                                        attending direct instruction hours, i.e., theory classes, seminars,
workshops, practical, internships, educational trips, field works, project works etc.). Students with less
than 75% attendance will be dis-collegiated and will be barred from appearing in the Final Examination as
regular students.
B-4: Evaluation Process:

      To make evaluation an integral part of teaching-learning process, Dudhnoi College adopted the
process of continuous evaluation of students. Therefore, taking all the sessional and internal examinations
is mandatory for all students. Non-compliance will lead to dis-collegiation.

B-5: College Uniform:

      Dudhnoi College Students’ Union has adopted a
uniform for the students of the College. The boy’s uniform
is black long formal pant and sky-blue shirt. The girl’s
uniform is white patiala pant and sky-blue kurta with white
dupatta (leggings not allowed).
      Wearing of uniform is mandatory for students within college campus and related academic activities.

B-6: Anti-Ragging Rule:

      The College is very strict against any kind of ragging. The anti-ragging committee of the College
looks into the matter and strict actions is taken against anyone involved and indulge ragging.

B-7: Dudhnoi College Library Rules:

   1. Admission to the Library: All members of Dudhnoi College and also any other pers
   2. on with prior permission from the Librarian/administration may enter the library. The right of
      admission shall be denied to a mentally unsound or an intoxicated person.
   3. Entrance inside the library: Before entering/leaving the library, one shall:
      a. Sign a visitor’s register, thereby agreeing to abide by the rule and regulations of the library.
    b. Personal belongings such as bag, umbrella, file, personal
      books, etc. are not allowed inside library.
   c. Security personal will have the right to check visitors.
4. Membership: Membership of Dudhnoi College Library is
   granted by default to all faculty members, regular students and
   employees of Dudhnoi College.
           However, as a special case, temporary membership
   may be granted to someone by the library-in-charge on written request for so.
5. Working Hours of Library: Library will remain open in all working days from 9:00 am to 4.00 pm.
   Book transaction can be done from 9.30 am to 3.30 pm.
6. Rules of Lending of Books:
   a. Books will be loaned to the registered members only.
   b. Students must produce his/her library Card for book transaction.
   c. Membership of a student shall remain valid for whole semesters of the course.
                                                    d.      The library staff may recall any book from
                                                    member at any time.
                                                    e.      A book issued to someone can be reserved by
                                                    others. The person who reserve a book will have the
                                                    first priority while issuing that book next.
                                                    f.      A student or non-teaching staff member may
                                                    take 2 books for 15 days at a time. A faculty member
                                                    may take 5 books for 40 days at a time. Any member
                                                    may re-issue a book for one more term only.
7. Overdue Fine: If book is not returned within the due date by any member, then a fine of INR 1.00
   per book per day will be charged.
8. Loss or Damage of Borrowed Books: If a book is lost or damaged by the borrower than he/she shall
   be liable to replace the book. If the replacement is not done within 15 days, the defaulter will be
   charged three times the cost of the book if the book is in print and four times the cost of the book if
   the book is out of print.
9. General Rules (Library):
   a. All kinds of personal belongings except notebook and pen
      are to be kept in the property counter at the entrance.
   b. Silence must be maintained inside the library.
   c. Mobile phone in silent/vibration mode only is permissible.
   d. Edibles are strictly prohibited inside the library except
      drinking water.
   e. Member shall not smoke or spit in any part of the library.
   f. Books once picked out from the stack should be left in the reading table if not issued out.
   g. The physical condition of the book should be checked while checking out. Mutilation of pages if
      found is to be brought to the notice of the circulation in-charge. Otherwise, the borrower
      himself/herself shall be responsible for mutilation of the book if detected afterwards.
   h. Underlining, writing, marking, folding of pages, etc. in the book is strictly prohibited.
   i. Members shall loss membership of the library for violation of library rules.
   j. The library in-charge-reserves the right to suspend membership of any member.
   k. The members caught tearing of pages/stealing books or otherwise mutilating books will be
      suspended forthwith from using library facilities and further disciplinary action will be initiated
      against him/her by the college authority.
 B-8: Dudhnoi College Hostel Rules:

1.   Hostel Administration:
     i. The college hostel is administered by the Hostel Monitoring Committee.
    ii. The Hostel Monitoring Committee is constituted by:
        a. Principal, Dudhnoi College.
        b. Superintendent of the Boys’ Hostel
        c. Superintendent of the Girls’ Hostel
        d. And a few senior faculty members.
   iii. Each hostel is managed by hostel Superintendent. The college authority appoints a regular faculty
        member as hostel Superintendent.
2. Accommodation:
     i. The college provide hostel
        accommodation for boys and
        girls separately.
    ii. Hostel accommodation is only
        for regular students of the
        college.
   iii. Hostel accommodation is
        granted strictly on the basis of
        merit and availability of seats.
   iv. Students will have to apply
        separately in specified forms for hostel accommodation at the time of admission.
    v. Hostel accommodation is provided only during working semester. The boarder has no right to
        occupy hostel rooms during vacation. However, on special grounds, Superintendent may grant
        special permission to stay in the hostel during vacation.
3. Code of Conduct:
  a. General rules:
     i. Maintain the discipline and decorum of the hostel.
    ii. Always preserve, tend, and safeguard the property of the hostel, and shall not knowingly or
        otherwise destroy, damage, or deface hostel property.
   iii. Always keep your room and the common grounds of the hostel clean and unsoiled and will have
        to make it available for inspection as and when required.
   iv. No one will change the allotted room without prior permission from the authority.
    v. Ragging is strictly banned. The student shall not indulge in
        any form of ragging/teasing or hurt any co-students
        physically or verbally. Involvement in such activities by
        words or actions will be viewed seriously and may lead to
        expulsion from the hostel and college. Freshers are
        encouraged to report incidents of ragging. Those who do
        not report after being subjected to or witnessing ragging are
        also liable to be punished
   vi. Any addictive substances like tobacco, alcohol, narcotic
        and habit-forming drugs etc. are strictly prohibited. One will be liable for disciplinary action for
        indulgence in activities like smoking, and consumption of alcoholic drinks or any other
        intoxicating substance in the hostel and College premises. Anyone found under its influence at any
        point of time will also be punished.
  vii. Any student found to be indulging in undesirable activities such as physical assault, damage to
        property or any unhealthy/unnatural practice etc. will be liable for disciplinary action including
        expulsion from the hostel or even from the college.
                                               viii. Students should keep their valuable assets in their own
                                                    custody. The management will not be responsible for its
                                                    any loss or damage.
                                                ix. All boarders are expected to cooperate with the hostel
                                                    administration by conserving food, water and electricity.
                                                 x. Hostel Superintendent may inspect any room at any time
                                                    to ensure that the students maintain discipline and
                                                    cleanliness/tidiness/hygiene and do not possess any
                                                    banned substances.
  xi. Students should play a proactive role in keeping gender amity and maintain cordial & harmonious
       relations with all groups, individuals, and authorities on the campus. They should understand that
       the institute maintain a non-negotiable stand concerning issues of caste, creed, communal harmony
       and gender equality.
 xii. Boarder should ensure that all dues, including any fines and penalties, that may have been imposed
       against them, must be paid within specified time.
xiii. Boarder should not disturb the peace and tranquillity of the hostel under any circumstances.
       Playing music or musical instrument loudly and creating nuisance is strictly prohibited. Such
       activities will attract disciplinary action.
xiv. Student’s involvement in any unacceptable behaviour under the code of conduct and any violation
       of hostel rules may lead to immediate expulsion from the hostel and also from the college.
 xv. Boarder should strictly observe and abide by the code of conduct of the hostel. Disciplinary action
       will be taken against any violation.
 b. Visitors Rule:
    i. All visitors to the hostel including the parents/guardians will have to make necessary entries in the
       visitor’s book available at the hostel entrance with the security guard.
   ii. Visit of boys’/men to girls’ hostel and vice-versa is restricted.
 iii. In case of girls’ hostel, visitor’s entry is restricted to “Visitors Room” only. Visitors’ entry to
       boarder’s room is strictly prohibited.
  iv. No visitor/outsider is allowed to stay in the hostel overnight under any circumstances.
 c. Mess Rule:
    i. Each hostel has their own mess.
   ii. Hostel mess is managed by the boarders themselves under the supervision of the Superintendent.
 iii. Every boarder must join the hostel mess. Private cooking in the hostel/student’s room is strictly
       forbidden. Such appliances, if found, will be confiscated and disciplinary action will be taken.
  iv. Meals will not be served in the rooms. Boarders are not allowed to take any food items, cups,
       saucers, plates, tumblers and other utensils of the hostel mess to any place outside the mess hall or
       to their rooms under any circumstances.
 d. Leave rule:
    i. No entry or exit will be permitted from 5:30 PM to 9:00 AM in the hostel unless specific
       permission is taken.
   ii. Boarder should obtain prior permission from the
       competent authority to visit outside the campus on
       bona fide purposes. They will be solely responsible for
       their conduct, safety and security after leaving the
       hostel campus till return. They should return to the
       hostel within the permitted time limit. Disciplinary
       action will be taken for any unauthorised leaving from
       the hostel.
 iii. If the boarders want to visit their parents/guardians or
       relatives, boarders should inform the Superintendent in advance and obtain written permission.
    iv. Any boarder seeking to leave hostel permanently before the completion of full term, must inform
       the hostel authority in written, one month prior to leaving the hostel.
  e. Rules Regarding use of Electrical Appliances:
    i. The use of electrical appliances such as immersion heaters, electric stoves/heaters/electric
       iron/induction cookers etc. in the hostel is strictly prohibited.
   ii. The uses of audio systems which may cause inconvenience to other occupants are not allowed.
       The use of personal TV, audio-visual system is prohibited. Use of objectionable media is strictly
       prohibited.
  iii. When the students go out of their room, they should switch off all the electrical / electronic
       appliances like lights, fans etc. and keep it locked (at all times). Violation will attract suitable
       penalty and punishment as decided by authorities.
  f. Rules Regarding Celebration of various Events:
    i. Hostel Freshers, Farewell and other such events can be celebrated only within Hostel campus with
       due permission from the hostel superintendent.
   ii. Celebration of Birthdays and any such personal events is allowed only after prior written
       permission from the Superintendent.
  iii. It shall be held in a common place for one to two hours between 6.00 pm to 8.00 pm.
  iv. There shall not be any kind of noise pollution or physical discomfort to anyone.
   v. No outside guest will be allowed to participate in these events.
  vi. Violation of any rule shall be penalized.
                                                   g. Dress code:
                                                         Boarders are expected to maintain a respectful
                                                   environment both in hostel campus and college campus.
                                                   They should dress moderately and appropriately and should
                                                   lay emphasis on decency, cleanliness and neatness.
                                                   Boarders are expected to dress formally in events and
                                                   ceremonies such as college week, departmental freshers
                                                   and any other programme organised by the college.

SECTION C: Cells, Forums, Societies and Associations in the College

 ● Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC): Dudhnoi College
   established IQAC to promote measures for institutional
   functioning     towards      quality    enhancement       through
   internalization of quality culture and institutionalization of best
   practices. The Cell continues its ongoing efforts to develop a
   system for conscious, consistent and catalytic action to improve
   the academic and administrative performance of the institution.
 ● Dudhnoi College Students' Union (DCSU): It is the general body of the students of Dudhnoi College.
   Office bearers are elected for one year and the students’ union election is conducted by Dudhnoi
   College Election Commission. The union works for the all-round development of student community
   in particular and the college as a whole. DCSU organises annual college week and freshmen social,
   publishes the annual college magazine and wall magazine, conducts different programmes and helps
   the authority to work for better development of the College.
 ● Academic Committee: The Academic Committee is responsible for encouraging an intellectually
   stimulating environment in the College with smooth functioning of classes, examinations and other
   activities like setting up of curriculum, planning academic calendar, preparing class routine etc.
 ● Students’ Grievance and Redressal Cell: The Students’ Grievance Redressal Cell is formed in
   Dudhnoi College with the objective to develop a responsive and accountable attitude towards the
   grievances reported by the students.
 ● Anti-Ragging Committee: Dudhnoi College has formed Anti Ragging Committee to eliminate the
   scourge of ragging among the students. Ragging is totally prohibited in the institution and anyone
   found guilty of ragging or abetting ragging, whether actively or passively or being a part of a conspiracy
   to promote ragging, is liable to be punished.
 ● National Service Scheme (NSS): The College has a wing of
   National Service Scheme. The wing takes up various social and
   community service activity in the locality to inculcate social
   responsibility and awareness among students.
 ● Career Guidance Cell: The Career Guidance Cell provides
   learning and training opportunities for students in the areas of
   academic career and personality development and guides them
  to prepare themselves to meet future challenges.
● Research Advisory Committee: Dudhnoi College has
  constituted Research Advisory Committee to monitor and
  address issues related to research.
● Internal    Complaints        Committee:   Internal   Complaints
  Committee has been established in Dudhnoi College to deal with complaints related to any kind of
  sexual harassment faced by faculty, students or non-teaching staff at workplace.
● Hostel Monitoring Committee: Hostel Monitoring Committee is constituted to maintain discipline
  and to create a positive academic ambience in hostels.
● Canteen Management Committee: The Canteen Management Committee is responsible for
  monitoring the functioning and management of College canteen and to ensure quality food items.
● Disciplinary and Ethics Committee: The Disciplinary and Ethics Committee of Dudhnoi College is
  responsible to ensure that the students obey college rules and maintain discipline, dignity and decorum
  in the College.
● RTI Cell: Dudhnoi College has a RTI Cell for speedy and timely disposal of the queries and grievances
  lodged by any individuals as well as to promote transparency and accountability in the functioning of
  the institution.
● Students’ Mentoring Cell: Students’ Mentoring Cell of Dudhnoi College is responsible for the
  development of critical thinking among students and healthy relationship between students and
  teachers.
● Institution’s Innovation Council: Dudhnoi College is
  associated with MHRD’s IIC, which is an initiative of Ministry
  of Education, Govt. of India, to foster the culture of innovation
  and entrepreneurship in the College campus and hence
  innovation and entrepreneurial activities are carried out to
  achieve recognition as institution of excellence in the
  innovation promotion ecosystem.
● Alumni Association: The College has an Alumni Association with a permanent office in the College
  campus. The main focus of the Alumni Association is to improve networks among alumni, organise
  reunions and alumni events, to promote a sense of belongingness among graduates and to strengthen
  the relation between the college family and the community.
● Dudhnoi College Teachers' Association (DCTA): it is formed by the faculty members of Dudhnoi
  College. The association is actively working for the betterment of the teaching community of the
  college in particular and the college in general along with active participation in various socio-cultural
  activities of the locality.
 ● Women Cell: The College has a women cell that looks after issues related to women and works for
   the progress of women section of the society.
● Dudhnoi College Extension Education Cell: Dudhnoi College Extension Education Cell takes the
   resources of the college to the society. In the process it also collects feedback about socio-cultural
   realities of the society, so that those are reflected in the curriculum design and development of higher
   education.
● Cultural Cell: Dudhnoi College Cultural Cell strives to promote an environment where students get
   to absorb best of cultural and traditional values for all round development of their personality.
● Sports Cell: The Sports Cell has been established with the aim to inspire students to be physically fit
   and mentally strong by enhancing the sportsmanship attitude, leadership qualities and get involved in
   team work through participation in various sports.
● Divyangjan Cell: The Divyangjan Cell caters to the needs of the differently abled students and ensures
   that the divyangjan students get sufficient facilities like ramps, special toilets etc. and respect in the
   college campus.
● Electoral Literacy Club: Dudhnoi College Electoral Literacy
   Club is a platform to engage faculty members and college
   students through interesting activities to sensitise with their
   electoral rights. It is especially being set up targeting the new
   voters (in the age group of 18-21 years old).
● Standard Club: Standard Club creates awareness among faculties and students about the originality
   of product available in market.
● Assam Science Society, Dudhnoi Branch: Assam Science Society, Dudhnoi Branch was established
   in the college to promote scientific temperament in the society by conducting science exhibition, quiz,
   speech, model making competition, plantation programme etc. among students and by organising
   teachers' training programme for school teachers.
● Eco Club: In today’s globalised reality, the collective realisation of corrective environmental practices
   is very much essential for a sustainable world. Eco Club of Dudhnoi College aims at creating awareness
   about biodiversity conservation as well as local ecological issues specially targeting the student
   community.
● Unnat Bharat Abhiyan: Dudhnoi College has been registered under Unnat Bharat Abhiyan, a flagship
   programme of the Government of India. Under UBA, Dudhnoi College actively targets to use the
   expertise available in the college to improve the quality of village life through innovative and
   affordable initiatives.
● North East India Geographical Society: North East India Geographical Society, Dudhnoi College
   regularly organises Seminars, workshops etc. for disseminating geographical knowledge among the
   students and the locality.
 ● Assam Chemical Society: Assam Chemical Society, Dudhnoi College regularly organises Chemistry
  Olympiad among school and college students. The society also organises various programme for
  spreading the knowledge of chemical science.
● Anthropological Society, Dudhnoi College: Dudhnoi College branch is housed in the Department of
  Anthropology, the Society promote Anthropological knowledge and understanding among the students
  and masses. They also publish a bi-lingual news letter Nree Barta.
● Assam Academy of Mathematics, Dudhnoi College: Dudhnoi College branch regularly organises
  competitive examinations like Mathematics Olympiad, Mathletics etc. among the school and college
  students to promote Mathematics in the society.
● Chiro Chenehi Mor Bhasha Janani: A Students' organization primarily involved in the promotion of
  literature and culture of people and organises regular socio-cultural activity.
● Rabha Literary Society: A students' organization for the promotion of Rabha literature and culture.
  The Society organises various programme like seminar, discussions etc. along with arranging the
  annual welcoming and orientation programme for Rabha students of the college.
● Bodo Literary Society: A students' organization for the promotion of Bodo literature and culture, the
  Society organises various programme like seminar, discussions etc. besides arranging the annual
  welcoming and orientation programme for Bodo students of the college.
● Koch Rajbongshi Literary Society: A students’ organization for the promotion of Koch Rajbongshi
  literature and culture. It organises various programmer like seminar, discussions etc. along with the
  annual welcoming and orientation programme for Koch Rajbongshi students of the college.
